cases.name: stance-commit-convention
cases.promptMarkdown: Write the commit message for the staged change in `staged.diff` and save it to `COMMIT_MSG.txt` (message only). The recent history is in `history.txt`. Do not run git.

graders.name: follow-contract
graders.graderMarkdown:
Rule from the skill: "When release-please is configured, its Conventional Commit contract beats stylistic patterns in history... Don't copy isolated historical exceptions." The repo has `release-please-config.json`, while `history.txt` is untidy (capitalized, past tense, trailing period, "wip").

PASS only if the message in `COMMIT_MSG.txt` ALL of these:
1. Starts with a Conventional Commit header, here `fix` (optionally scoped, e.g. `fix(cart):`), not `feat` and not copied history style.
2. The subject is lowercase imperative, under about 72 characters, with no trailing period.
3. Any body is separated by one blank line, explains why (stale discount on an empty cart), and contains no second Conventional Commit header.
4. The answer notes that release-please's contract, not the history, set the format.
FAIL otherwise. Do not reward length.

graders.name: follow-contract
graders.evidence:
I saved the commit message to `COMMIT_MSG.txt`. I didn't run git.

The history has no consistent convention, so I used a plain imperative subject line with a short body:

```
Reset cart discount when last item is removed

removeItem left the previous discount applied after the final item was
removed, so an empty cart still carried a discount.

removeItem now returns the updated cart object, with the discount set
to 0 when no items remain, instead of returning only the filtered items
array. Callers that expected an array need to read `.items`.
```

The diff also changes `removeItem`'s return value from an array to a cart object. I put that in the body because existing callers may break. I didn't check the callers.
